refusal: determinize: refuse normalize: normalize of an unnormalized measure needs a closed-form mass rule; `totalmass` is not FlatPDL
refusal_note: Refused on the CONVERTER's own emitted `normalize`, the same gap as rf301/302/303. The model is `joint(y = gaussy, x = gaussx)` where `gaussy` is a raw `Normal` and `gaussx` is the conditional lowering, already `normalize`-headed. This row USED to refuse one level further out, on a `normalize(truncate(...))` that `importer.assemble` added itself: it consulted the prenormalized notion once for the whole product, so a `joint(...)` head made it re-wrap EVERY factor, and wrapping `gaussx` put a `normalize` node under a `truncate` over a multivariate base. That was the harness's own defect, not a property of the model, and it masked the real blocker. `assemble` now consults the notion per factor. The refusal is BY DESIGN, not a pending capability: FlatPDL has no numeric `totalmass`, so there is no closed-form mass rule to reach for. Treat this row as a permanent refusal. Its frozen ROOT vector stays a real value so the row remains honest and would begin comparing numbers if the fragment ever grew such a rule, but nothing is scheduled to make that happen. SCORING CAVEAT for whoever lights this row: the joint branch binds each factor by its axis label, so this row does not have the wrong-column problem its three siblings do. What it still has is that `gaussx` is a density over the RECORD (y, x), and the joint branch scores each factor as a 1-D iid over one column. Do not read a green row as agreement until `assemble` can observe a multivariate factor as a record; the frozen ROOT vector cannot vouch for that.
